h1: Private Jet to Acapulco from Mexico City
hero_sub: The bay curves like an amphitheater, divers leap from La Quebrada at dusk, and the Pacific is closer than your Friday traffic.
answer: A private jet to Acapulco takes about 45 minutes from Toluca (AIT) to Acapulco International (ACA), and starts at $1,500 USD one way per aircraft. Other aircraft are quoted in 30 minutes. The price covers the whole aircraft with crew, fuel, catering and permits included. Compared with about four hours on the Autopista del Sol, it is the quickest way from the capital to the Pacific.
story: Long before Cancún existed, Acapulco was where the world came to the beach. In the 1950s and 60s, film stars married and honeymooned on the bay, Frank Sinatra sang about it, and the cliff divers of La Quebrada became one of the most photographed sights in Mexico. The bay itself is a near-perfect curve of sand backed by green hills, and from the heights of Las Brisas at night the city lights wrap around the water like the seats of an amphitheater.

The city has three faces. Old Acapulco, around the zócalo and La Quebrada, keeps the life of a traditional port. The Costera Miguel Alemán follows the main bay with its hotels and nightlife. Acapulco Diamante, out near the airport, is the newer area of resorts, villas and the long, open beach of Revolcadero.
why_title: Why fly a private jet to Acapulco

why.d: The drive from Mexico City to Acapulco takes about four hours on a good day and far longer on a holiday weekend. A private jet to Acapulco covers the trip in about 45 minutes in the air, so Friday traffic stops being part of your weekend.

At 45 minutes each way, you can fly down for lunch at a villa, a family celebration or a property visit and be back in Toluca the same evening. Domestic flights can be ready about 2 hours after you confirm on WhatsApp.

Bring the golf clubs, the beach gear and enough luggage for a week. Everything travels with you on the aircraft, and the cabin belongs to your group alone, from the grandparents to the youngest child, for the entire flight.

Flights start at $1,500 USD one way, per aircraft, with crew, fuel, catering and permits included. Larger aircraft for bigger groups are quoted in 30 minutes, and the price you see covers everyone on board, with no per-seat charges.

journey_title: Friday afternoon, Mexico City to the bay

journey.d: Instead of joining the line of cars heading south on the Autopista del Sol, your driver takes the México-Toluca highway west, about an hour to the airport. An official photo ID is all anyone needs for this domestic flight.

The car pulls up at the private terminal (FBO) at Toluca International. A quick ID check, your bags go aboard, and you are at the aircraft steps in under 10 minutes from the curb. Cold drinks are ready on board.

The flight crosses the ridges of the Sierra Madre del Sur and the deep valleys of Guerrero. You barely have time to finish a drink before the descent begins and the coastline appears through the window, bright against the blue.

You touch down at Acapulco International after about 45 minutes. Guerrero runs on Mexico City time. Your car is waiting on the private aviation side, and the warm, humid air reaches you as soon as the door opens.

Fifteen minutes takes you to the resorts of Acapulco Diamante, about thirty to the main bay. By sunset you are on a terrace in Las Brisas with a cold drink, watching the lights of the bay come on one by one.

places_title: What to do in Acapulco after you land

places.name: La Quebrada Cliff Divers
places.d: Since the 1930s, the divers of La Quebrada have leapt from ledges up to 35 meters high into a narrow ocean inlet, timing each dive to the incoming swell. Watch the evening shows from the public viewing platform or from a terrace above the cove as the light fades.

places.name: Fort of San Diego
places.d: Built to protect the Manila galleons that sailed between Acapulco and the Philippines, this star-shaped fort now houses the Acapulco Historical Museum. Its ramparts offer one of the best views over the old port and the bay, and the exhibits tell the story of the Pacific trade route.

places.name: Pie de la Cuesta
places.d: A strip of sand between the open Pacific and the Coyuca Lagoon, about 30 minutes northwest of the old town. The surf is too strong for swimming, so come for hammocks, grilled fish and one of the best sunsets on the coast, then take a boat out on the calm lagoon.

places.name: Puerto Marqués
places.d: A small, sheltered bay next to Acapulco Diamante, with calm water that suits children and a row of palapa restaurants serving pescado a la talla, the grilled fish of Guerrero. It is only a few minutes from the airport, which makes it a perfect first lunch on the coast.

best_time_title: Best time to fly to Acapulco
best_time: Acapulco is warm all year, and the water stays warm enough to swim in every month. The dry season from November to April is the best time to go, with clear skies and very little rain. It is also when Mexico City families fill the villas, especially at Christmas, New Year and Semana Santa, and the long holiday weekends in February, March and November get busy too, so send your dates early for those. June to October is rainy and humid, and the Pacific hurricane season runs from mid-May through November. A private jet to Acapulco keeps flying all year.
airport: Acapulco International (ACA), officially General Juan N. Álvarez International, sits about 350 km from Toluca on the eastern edge of the city, in the Acapulco Diamante zone. Private aircraft are handled in the general aviation area, apart from the commercial terminal, and your car can meet you there. Puerto Marqués and the Diamante resorts are 10 to 15 minutes away, the Costera and the main bay about 30 minutes, Old Acapulco and La Quebrada around 40, and Pie de la Cuesta about an hour. This is a domestic flight, so there is no customs.
docs_title: Documents for a private flight to Acapulco
docs: Your flight to Acapulco is domestic, so Mexican nationals only need a valid official photo ID, such as an INE card or a passport. Foreign visitors should carry the passport they used to enter Mexico. Send the full name of every passenger on WhatsApp when you confirm, and the aircraft can be ready about 2 hours later. Customs and immigration do not apply on this route.

faq.q: Is Acapulco open after Hurricane Otis?
faq.a: Yes. Acapulco has been rebuilding since Hurricane Otis in October 2023, and many hotels, restaurants and beach clubs have reopened. Recovery varies from property to property, so confirm your hotel or villa directly before you fly. JETCAB flies the Toluca to Acapulco route 365 days a year.
